description.description: Brief description of the visual interpretation in the user's language.

code.description: Complete async function expression async function(PIXI, app, api) { ... return {update, resize?, setData?, pointer?, dispose?}; }. PixiJS v8 API only (Graphics: g.moveTo().lineTo().stroke({color,width}); g.circle(x,y,r).fill({color}); new PIXI.Text({text, style})). frame.fields is a FLAT map whose keys are exactly the keys of initialSolverFields (e.g. frame.fields['car.position']); reading any other key throws. Never solve physics in drawing code: every moving quantity comes from frame.fields. Recommended structure: (1) const base = api.kit.standardScene({bodies: false}) gives a measured coordinate frame fitted to the full solver ranges, axes/ruler with SI units, trajectories, strobe marks, velocity/acceleration/force vectors, labels and a time HUD; (2) add contextual artwork (original SVG through await api.svgTexture(svg) where svg is a complete <svg viewBox=...> document) as sprites; (3) in update(frame) call base.update(frame) then place each sprite at base.screenOf(modelId, frame.fields) (returns {x,y} screen pixels or null). Call base.resize() from resize and base.setData() from setData. Other helpers: api.kit.palette() (theme-aware colours: ink, muted, grid, axis, halo, velocity, acceleration, force, series[]), api.kit.color(i), api.kit.camera(viewRect, worldBounds, equalScale) -> {toScreen(x,y), sx, sy}, api.kit.arrow(g, x1, y1, x2, y2, {color, width}), api.kit.text(str, {size, color, weight}), api.kit.format(value, unit), api.kit.participants() (id, label, dims, fields), api.getFieldRanges() (min/max over the whole run; recompute layout in resize/setData, never hard-code ranges). Use theme-aware colours from api.kit.palette() so text stays readable in light and dark workspaces; keep all content inside api.width x api.height. No imports, networking, DOM, eval, external assets, own ticker or application.
